name: Aave
purpose: Pooled lending market: suppliers earn interest through aTokens, borrowers take variable-rate loans against collateral, unhealthy positions are liquidated.
about: One Pool per market holds the books for every reserve (asset). The Pool itself is thin: each action is delegated to an external logic library (SupplyLogic, BorrowLogic, LiquidationLogic, FlashLoanLogic) that runs on the Pool's storage. Liquidity sits in each reserve's aToken; debt is a non-transferable VariableDebtToken. Interest accrues through two indexes per reserve (liquidity and variable borrow), moved forward on every action. Prices come from AaveOracle; roles from ACLManager; addresses of everything from PoolAddressesProvider.

flows.title: Supply
flows.summary: Deposit an asset, receive aTokens that grow with interest.

steps.say: Approves the Pool for the asset, then calls supply(asset, amount, onBehalfOf, referralCode).
Entry point. Passes the reserve and user books to SupplyLogic.
Runs by DELEGATECALL, so every write lands in the Pool's storage.
Accrues interest since the last action: moves the liquidity and variable borrow indexes to now and books the treasury's share.
Amount not zero; reserve active, not paused, not frozen; supply cap not exceeded; onBehalfOf is not the aToken itself.
Adds the amount to the reserve's virtual balance and asks the rate strategy for new rates.
The underlying moves from the supplier straight into the aToken contract, which holds the reserve's liquidity.
Mints the amount divided by the liquidity index (scaled balance) to onBehalfOf.
On a first supply, decides whether the asset is switched on as collateral automatically (an isolated asset only when the supplier holds the isolated collateral supplier role).
Emits Supply(reserve, user, onBehalfOf, amount, referralCode).

checks: Indexes are updated before any amount is scaled, so the minted scaled amount uses the current liquidity index.
The scaled amount rounds down on mint (rayDivFloor), in the protocol's favour.
The supply cap is checked against the scaled total supply plus the treasury's accrued share.
Integrations: the aToken balance changes every block; read it, don't cache it.

flows.title: Borrow
flows.summary: Take a variable-rate loan against supplied collateral.

steps.say: Calls borrow(asset, amount, interestRateMode = variable, referralCode, onBehalfOf). onBehalfOf other than the caller needs a credit delegation allowance.
Entry point. Reads the oracle and the sentinel from PoolAddressesProvider.
Runs on the Pool's storage.
Accrues interest to now.
Reserve active, not paused or frozen, borrowing enabled, borrow cap, isolation mode debt ceiling, siloed borrowing, e-mode, and the oracle sentinel's grace period.
Records the debt: amount divided by the variable borrow index. Spends the credit delegation allowance when onBehalfOf is someone else.
Takes the amount out of the virtual balance and recomputes rates.
The aToken sends the underlying to the borrower.
After the transfer: totals collateral and debt at oracle prices and requires health factor above 1 and the new LTV within limits. If not, the whole transaction reverts.
Price of every asset in the account, read inside the health factor computation.
Emits Borrow with the current variable rate.

checks: The health factor is checked after funds leave; the check must cover every state change made before it.
Every price comes from AaveOracle: check each asset's source, its decimals, and what happens when it returns 0 (fallback oracle).
Credit delegation: borrowing onBehalfOf spends an allowance on the debt token, not on the aToken.
Isolation mode and siloed borrowing restrict which assets can be borrowed together; confirm both are enforced on every path that mints debt (borrow and flashLoan with a debt mode).

flows.title: Repay
flows.summary: Pay back variable debt with the underlying (or with aTokens).

steps.say: Approves the Pool, then calls repay(asset, amount, interestRateMode, onBehalfOf). type(uint256).max repays the whole debt.
Entry point. repayWithATokens takes the same path with useATokens = true.
Runs on the Pool's storage.
Accrues interest to now, so the debt includes interest up to this block.
Amount not zero, reserve active and not paused, there is debt to repay. max is only allowed when repaying for yourself.
Burns the repaid amount, capped at the outstanding debt; clears the borrowing flag when nothing is left.
Adds the payment back to the virtual balance and recomputes rates.
The payment moves from the payer into the aToken. With aTokens, the payer's aTokens are burned instead.
Emits Repay(reserve, user, repayer, amount, useATokens).

checks: The amount actually taken is the lesser of the request and the debt; integrations should read the return value, not assume the requested amount.
Repaying with aTokens reduces collateral too, so the health factor is re-checked when other debt remains.
Debt burns round the scaled amount down (less debt removed, in the protocol's favour); repaying with type(uint256).max must still clear the debt to zero.

flows.title: Liquidation
flows.summary: Close part of an unhealthy position: repay its debt, receive its collateral with a bonus.

steps.say: Calls liquidationCall(collateralAsset, debtAsset, borrower, debtToCover, receiveAToken) after approving the debt asset.
Entry point. Passes the oracle and sentinel addresses to LiquidationLogic.
Runs on the Pool's storage.
Accrues interest on both the debt reserve and the collateral reserve.
Recomputes the borrower's collateral, debt and health factor at current prices.
No self-liquidation; both reserves active and not paused; sentinel and grace period allow it; health factor below 1; the collateral is enabled and liquidatable; the borrower has this debt.

Prices of the collateral and the debt asset, used to size the collateral to seize with the liquidation bonus. Up to 50% of the debt can be covered in one call; 100% when the health factor is below 0.95 or the position is small.
Burns the covered debt. If no collateral would remain, the rest is burned too and booked as reserve deficit.
Collateral to the liquidator: underlying (aTokens burned) or, with receiveAToken, the aTokens themselves.
The liquidation protocol fee, a share of the bonus, goes to the treasury in aTokens.
The liquidator's payment in the debt asset moves into the debt reserve's aToken.
Emits LiquidationCall with the debt covered and collateral seized.

checks: Liquidation is a designed safety valve; review that the close factor, bonus and protocol fee are applied in the documented order and rounding favours the protocol.
Every number depends on two oracle prices read in the same transaction: check each feed's freshness and decimals assumptions.
Deficit handling: debt burned without collateral must be recorded exactly once and only for positions with no collateral left.
Integrations that hold Aave positions must keep their health factor monitored; their own accounting must survive a partial liquidation.

flows.title: Flash loan
flows.summary: Borrow liquidity within one transaction; pay it back with a premium before it ends.

steps.say: A contract calls flashLoanSimple(receiverAddress, asset, amount, params, referralCode).
Entry point. Reads the premium set by governance.
Runs on the Pool's storage.
Reserve active, not paused, flash loans enabled, and the amount within the aToken's supply.
Sends the amount to the receiver; the virtual balance is reduced first.
The receiver's own code runs, with the amount and the premium owed. It must return true.
Repayment: accrues interest and books the premium for the treasury.
Pulls amount plus premium from the receiver back into the aToken. Without the approval, the whole transaction reverts.
Emits FlashLoan with the premium paid.

checks: Liquidity leaves and must return in the same transaction; review that every state read during executeOperation is either final or re-read after repayment.
Receivers: executeOperation must check msg.sender is the Pool and initiator is trusted, since anyone can start a flash loan to any receiver.
Flash borrowers registered in ACLManager pay no premium on flashLoan (flashLoanSimple always charges it); that role should be held only by known contracts.
Access: list who holds each ACLManager role and the PoolAddressesProvider owner; they can change any parameter or implementation.
Oracles: every asset's price source, its heartbeat and decimals, and the fallback oracle path.
Index math: scaled balances and the order of updateState before any scaling, on every action.
Library code runs on the Pool's storage: review storage layout compatibility on every Pool upgrade.
Integrations: aToken balances rebase; debt tokens can't be transferred; repay may take less than requested.
notes: Mapped: the Pool, its configurator and logic libraries, both tokens, registry, roles, oracle and rate strategy. Not mapped: periphery (rewards, gateways, data providers, StataToken), GHO, governance.
